name: The everyday classic
heading: Libre Baskerville
use: Recommended starting point: Sunday bulletins, welcome pages, and the main website.
note: A traditional serif paired with an unobtrusive, readable sans. Keeps the church voice warm without feeling ornamental.
evidence: Reddit recommends these families individually; this exact pairing is our editorial recommendation.

name: The gentle editorial
heading: Lora
use: Pastoral letters, ministry stories, invitations, and longer reading.
note: A softer serif and a humanist sans. A calm alternative with more warmth than a geometric headline.
evidence: A commenter in the linked r/typography resume discussion explicitly recommends Lato + Lora.

name: The practical reader
heading: Merriweather
use: Weekly announcements, service information, and text-heavy print pieces.
note: A sturdy serif with an open sans for schedules and details. Strong default for information people need to read quickly.
evidence: Reddit discussions recommend Merriweather and Open Sans as workhorse families; the exact combination is our recommendation.

name: The confident welcome
heading: Montserrat
use: Event headlines, homepage sections, ministry brochures, and invitations.
note: Structured sans headings with a warmer serif body. Use Montserrat sparingly; its wide letters need breathing room.
evidence: Reddit mentions Montserrat as versatile, with some commenters calling it overused. The pairing is our recommendation.

name: The quiet modern
heading: Raleway
use: Web landing pages, simple flyers, information cards, and email graphics.
note: A lightly expressive sans headline over a familiar body face. Keep Raleway at semibold or bold rather than thin weights.
evidence: This exact combination appears in Canva’s Google font pairing guide; Reddit provides broader support for Open Sans.

name: The all-purpose system
heading: Montserrat
use: Wayfinding, foyer screens, web navigation, and social announcements.
note: A direct sans-serif system. The headline weight and scale do the work; the body stays quiet and legible.
evidence: Both families are recommended in community discussions. Exact combination selected for CPC’s practical use cases.

name: The special occasion
heading: Playfair Display
use: Seasonal services, concert invitations, and short editorial headlines.
note: High-contrast serif headings bring ceremony. Keep Playfair large and use Lato for every practical detail.
evidence: An editorial recommendation based on contrast and use case, not a claim of Reddit consensus on this exact pair.

name: The poster voice
heading: Oswald
use: Foyer posters, registration calls, youth events, and short social headlines.
note: Condensed headings fit limited space. Avoid long all-caps paragraphs; keep the body open and normal width.
evidence: Canva features Oswald and Open Sans in its font guides. The exact combination is our recommendation.

name: The literary invitation
heading: Libre Baskerville
use: Lecture series, printed invitations, sermon-series titles, and event cards.
note: Bookish headings with crisp geometric details. Use Montserrat regular for short copy, not dense multi-page reading.
evidence: Canva and Reddit recommend the families; their combination here is an editorial choice.
